projects.title: DSCASC — Class Representative Election Platform
projects.tagline: Secure online platform for class representative elections
projects.summary: The system provides an institutional web application for conducting class representative elections. It supports multiple independent elections, each with its own candidates, authorities, votes, results and schedule. Users interact through role‑aware dashboards for admins, teachers, candidates and students.
projects.problem: Educational institutions need a reliable way to run internal elections that prevents duplicate voting, protects vote secrecy, and applies weighted voting rules across different stakeholder groups.
howItWorks: Users sign in with Google via Firebase Authentication and receive a role claim validated against invitation records.
The Next.js front end renders role‑specific pages and communicates with Cloud Firestore, where elections, candidates, and votes are stored.
Vote documents are created with a Firestore transaction and cannot be updated or deleted, ensuring a single vote per user.
Candidate profile images are uploaded directly to Cloudinary after obtaining a server‑signed request from an API route.
Results are calculated from stored votes using a weighted formula and written to a protected result document.
QR codes link to public election pages but still require authenticated access before voting.
highlights: Immutable vote documents enforce one‑time voting even across page refreshes or multiple tabs.
Firestore security rules restrict data access by role and enforce admin email checks on the server side.
Server‑only Cloudinary signing keeps API secrets out of the browser.
Weighted result logic combines student votes (70%) with authority votes (10% each) per gender category.
RoleGuard component and server rules together protect admin and teacher dashboards.

projects.title: Code Port
projects.tagline: Resume builder that generates previews, PDFs, and 3D portfolio sites via AI interview.
projects.summary: Code Port lets users create a resume through a guided AI interview. The app provides a live‑updating preview, a server‑generated PDF download, and an animated 3D portfolio website. It targets users who want a modern, interactive presentation of their work.
howItWorks: The front end is built with Next.js App Router and renders the UI with React components.
User responses are collected via a guided AI interview that calls the GROQ API when an API key is provided, otherwise a deterministic local flow is used.
Responses are stored in Supabase, which also supplies data for the live preview.
The preview updates in real time and can be exported as a PDF using React PDF on the server.
An animated 3D portfolio is rendered with React Three Fiber and Drei, with motion handled by Framer Motion.
highlights: Falls back to a deterministic local interview flow when the GROQ API key is missing.
Generates a server‑side PDF of the resume using React PDF.

projects.title: Pow Protocol

projects.summary: A Next.js 16 project using TypeScript, React 19, and Tailwind CSS. Integrates Firebase for backend services, Octokit for GitHub API access, and Chart.js with Mermaid for data visualization and diagramming.
howItWorks: Built on Next.js App Router with TypeScript
Uses Firebase for authentication and data storage
Communicates with GitHub via Octokit REST client

projects.title: Yogstra
projects.tagline: Premium yoga ecosystem platform for teachers, academies, and participants
projects.summary: Yogstra is a web platform that lets users discover yoga teachers, enroll in programs, run academies, and host competitions. It combines class management, payment processing, and live video streaming in a single service.
howItWorks: The frontend is built with React 19, Vite, and Tailwind CSS, using React Router for navigation.
Supabase provides Postgres storage, authentication, file storage, and realtime capabilities for the backend.
Razorpay is integrated for payments and includes a route for teacher payouts.
LiveKit Cloud supplies video streaming for live classes and events.
The application is deployed on Vercel and uses TypeScript throughout the codebase.
highlights: Full‑stack architecture centered on Supabase for database, auth, and realtime features.
Integrated payment flow with Razorpay, including teacher payout handling.
Live video support via LiveKit Cloud for real‑time yoga sessions.
End‑to‑end testing with Playwright and accessibility checks using @axe-core/playwright.
Linting with oxlint and modern build pipeline using Vite.

projects.title: Quintyx
projects.tagline: Systematic quantitative investing website with admin dashboard
projects.summary: Quintyx Capital Management's web presence presents information about its systematic quantitative investing approach, philosophy, risk disclosure, and investor resources. The site includes a separate admin dashboard for internal content management. It is built with standard web technologies and hosted on Vercel.
projects.problem: The firm needed a public-facing site to communicate its investment strategy and related information, as well as an internal interface for managing site content.
howItWorks: Static pages are authored in HTML and styled with CSS.
Interactive elements and the admin dashboard are powered by JavaScript.
The site is organized into multiple HTML files (e.g., index.html, about.html, investors.html).
Deployment configuration is defined in vercel.json, enabling hosting on Vercel.
Admin.html provides a dedicated interface for managing site content.
highlights: Separate admin.html page serves as a lightweight dashboard for content updates.
Configured for Vercel deployment using vercel.json and .vercelignore.

projects.title: QR Code Generator
projects.tagline: A Next.js web app for creating QR codes
projects.summary: The project is a web application built with Next.js that lets users generate QR codes. It provides a form for input and renders the corresponding QR image, which can be exported as an image file. The interface is styled with Tailwind CSS and uses React components for interactivity.
howItWorks: The app runs on the Next.js framework with TypeScript for type safety.
User input is managed by react-hook-form and validated with Zod.
QR codes are rendered using the qrcode.react library.
The generated QR image can be captured as a PNG using html-to-image.
Styling and layout are handled with Tailwind CSS and shadcn UI components.
highlights: Built with Next.js 16 and TypeScript.
Uses Tailwind CSS for utility‑first styling.
Integrates shadcn UI components for consistent design.
Employs react-hook-form with Zod for form handling and validation.

projects.title: Voca
projects.tagline: Free AI voice dictation for macOS
projects.summary: Voca lets macOS users dictate text by holding the Fn key. The spoken input is transcribed, cleaned, and inserted at the cursor in any application. It also supports quick Q&A with an on‑screen answer popup.
projects.problem: Typing extended passages or technical terms can be time‑consuming, and existing dictation tools often insert raw speech with filler words and incorrect spelling. Voca addresses the need for accurate, formatted text directly from voice input.
howItWorks: When the user holds Fn, Voca records lossless audio and sends it to Whisper large‑v3 via the configured Groq (or fallback) API.
The transcription is passed to an AI cleanup step that corrects grammar, punctuation, and applies a user‑defined vocabulary list.
The cleaned text is typed into the active window using macOS accessibility services; if permission is missing, the text is copied to the clipboard.
Holding Fn + Shift sends the audio to the same model for a short answer, which appears in a Liquid Glass popup without typing.
A double‑tap on Fn locks recording for longer dictations, and a 24‑hour history lets the user paste, copy, or retry previous entries.
highlights: Native Swift executable targeting macOS 26+, using about 40 MB of RAM.
Falls back to on‑device Apple speech recognizer when no API key is available.
Liquid Glass UI with live waveform and configurable microphone selection.
History stored locally for 24 hours and automatically deleted.
Build and install scripts are provided in Shell for quick setup.

projects.title: Prompt Labs
projects.tagline: A precision monochrome instrument for reusable AI prompts.
projects.summary: Prompt Labs lets users capture, organize, discover, customize, reuse and share AI prompts through a monochrome dot‑matrix interface. The web app stores prompts locally or in Firebase and supports collections, favorites, export and publishing.
howItWorks: At runtime the app selects a data backend: Firebase when configured with Email/Password enabled, otherwise a local browser adapter that uses localStorage.
The UI is built with Next.js 16.4 (App Router, Turbopack), React 19, TypeScript and Tailwind CSS v4.
Prompt data is accessed through adapters in src/lib/adapters, abstracted by a Backend interface.
Client state (auth, prompts, collections, favorites, recents, toasts) is managed in src/lib/store.tsx.
Dot‑matrix visual components are provided in src/components/dots and used throughout the interface.
All user journeys across 12 screens are verified with Playwright end‑to‑end tests.
highlights: Runtime backend resolution with a transparent localStorage fallback and a visible banner indicating the active backend.
Seeded demo account and synthetic public prompts for immediate exploration in local mode.
Explicit privacy defaults: prompts are private unless explicitly published, enforced by Firestore security rules.
Export of the entire library as JSON for migration or backup.
Full end‑to‑end test coverage (16 journeys, desktop and mobile) using Playwright.

projects.title: RepoBank
projects.tagline: GitHub repository library and discovery platform
projects.summary: RepoBank lets users save public GitHub repositories, add notes, tags, and organize them with a kanban workflow. Collections can be kept private or published for public discovery. The service runs on Vercel's free tier and Firebase's Spark plan.
projects.problem: Developers often need a way to track repositories beyond simple name search, preserving context such as notes, status, and categorisation while being able to share curated lists with others.
howItWorks: The front end is built with Next.js 16 (App Router) and Tailwind CSS, delivering a minimal black‑and‑white UI.
When a user saves a repository URL, the server fetches metadata from the GitHub API and stores it in a public Firestore cache.
User‑specific data—status, notes, tags, collection membership—is kept in a private Firestore sub‑collection keyed by the Firebase UID.
Authentication uses Firebase Email/Password from the shared Prompt Labs project, so existing accounts sign in directly.
Optional AI summarisation can be enabled with an OpenAI key; otherwise a deterministic classifier provides tag suggestions.
The kanban board supports drag‑and‑drop as well as keyboard controls, and all pages are built with accessible HTML patterns.
highlights: Reuses the existing Prompt Labs Firebase project, avoiding duplicate authentication infrastructure.
Runs entirely on free tiers (Vercel Hobby, Firebase Spark) and does not require an AI API key by default.
Server‑side GitHub metadata fetch is cached to prevent repeated API calls during rendering.
Public explore and collection pages are designed to never expose private notes or library records.
Bulk import supports CSV/JSON with preview, idempotent writes, and progress reporting.
Accessibility features include semantic HTML, visible focus indicators, reduced‑motion support, and keyboard navigation.

projects.title: NBOOK
projects.tagline: A tactile, archival digital notebook with hierarchical blocks and access-key authentication
projects.summary: NBOOK is a self-hosted digital notebook organized as Book → Chapter → Page → Block. It uses access keys instead of accounts, supports real-time collaboration over SSE, and runs with zero configuration via a local JSON fallback.
projects.problem: Traditional note-taking tools require accounts, lack fine-grained hierarchy, and often conflate editing with execution. NBOOK addresses this by providing a tactile, archival writing environment with role-based access keys, optimistic concurrency, and a block model that separates content from computation.
howItWorks: Data is modeled as a four-level hierarchy: books contain chapters, chapters contain pages, pages contain ordered blocks.
A StorageDriver interface abstracts persistence; FirestoreDriver and LocalDriver (JSON file) implement it, scoped by bookId.
Access keys (owner, editor, viewer) are hashed at rest and exchanged for signed, httpOnly session cookies with 12-hour expiry.
Real-time updates flow over SSE for tree changes, block edits, and presence; block writes use optimistic concurrency with rev/baseRev and 409 rebase-retry.
The UI layer uses Tiptap for rich text, CodeMirror 6 for code blocks with Shiki highlighting, and tldraw for canvas blocks.
AI Assist routes requests through Groq then OpenRouter, degrading gracefully when keys are absent.
highlights: Zero-configuration local fallback (`.nbook-data/db.json`) enables immediate use without Firebase credentials.
Access-key model: keys are never stored in plaintext; revocation stops future unlocks but respects existing sessions until cookie expiry.
Optimistic concurrency on blocks with automatic rebase-retry on conflict (409).
Tactile design system: paper grain, spine gutter, folio sheets, synthesized page-turn rustle respecting `prefers-reduced-motion`, three themes and three font scales.
Full i18n with RTL support for English, Kannada, and Arabic.
Comprehensive test strategy: Vitest unit suites, Playwright e2E suite driving real Chromium, and Firestore emulator integration tests.

projects.title: AI Browser Harness
projects.tagline: Grant specific Chrome tabs to AI agents via MCP and a local HTTP API
projects.summary: AI Browser Harness lets you share individual Chrome tabs with AI agents such as Cursor, Claude, or ChatGPT. A sidecar process provides a local MCP server and optional public tunnel, while a Chrome extension enforces tab-level permissions. The CLI (`./agenth`) manages pairing, token generation, and tab sharing.
projects.problem: Developers and users need a way to let AI agents act on web pages while keeping the rest of the browser private.
howItWorks: A Chrome extension is built and loaded as an unpacked extension.
Running `./agenth` starts a sidecar that hosts a local MCP HTTP server and, if cloudflared is installed, a public HTTPS tunnel.
The sidecar generates a pairing token stored in `~/.ai-browser-harness/config.json`.
The user pairs the extension with the sidecar using the token, then shares specific tabs through the extension UI.
AI agents connect to the MCP endpoint (local or tunneled) and can invoke tools such as `tabs_list`, `click`, or `snapshot` only on the granted tabs.
highlights: Uses a token‑based authentication model for MCP connections.
Supports optional Cloudflare tunnel to reach cloud‑based AI services.
Provides a TUI for managing pairing, token, and tunnel status.
CLI includes commands for building the extension, opening the build folder, and serving the sidecar.

projects.title: Birthday Gift Studio
projects.tagline: Create a personalized birthday website from a short form
projects.summary: Birthday Gift Studio lets users answer a few questions about a friend and instantly generates a custom birthday website. The site includes an unwrap animation, confetti celebration, and a shareable link. It is intended for anyone who wants a quick, personalized birthday page without building it from scratch.
howItWorks: The user opens the Next.js application and fills out a short questionnaire about the birthday person.
Form data is validated with Zod and stored using Vercel Blob.
A unique URL is generated with nanoid and the site is rendered on the fly using React components.
Framer Motion provides the unwrap animation, while canvas-confetti adds celebratory confetti effects.
The resulting page can be shared via the generated link.
highlights: Built with Next.js 16 and TypeScript for server‑rendered React pages.
Uses Tailwind CSS for styling and layout.
Integrates canvas-confetti for visual effects and Framer Motion for animations.
Employs Zod for schema‑based form validation.
Leverages Vercel Blob for lightweight data storage.

projects.title: Visual Code Lab
projects.tagline: A Next.js app for visualizing complex code and simplifying it.
projects.summary: Visual Code Lab is a web application built with Next.js that lets users view complex source code and refactor it into a shorter form. It provides an interactive editor powered by Monaco and visualizations via Mermaid, aimed at developers who want to streamline code.
projects.problem: Developers often need to understand and reduce large, complex codebases, which can be time‑consuming.
howItWorks: The front end is a Next.js application written in TypeScript and React.
Code is displayed and edited using the Monaco Editor component.
Mermaid renders diagrammatic representations of code structures.
Framer Motion adds animated transitions for a smoother user experience.
Client‑side data such as user preferences is stored with idb-keyval.
Zod validates data structures throughout the app.
highlights: Integration of Monaco Editor for a full‑featured code editing experience.
Use of Mermaid to generate visual diagrams from code.
Client‑side persistence via IndexedDB through idb-keyval.

projects.title: Nexus Last-Mile Route Optimizer & Late-Delivery Risk Predictor
projects.tagline: A route planner with ML‑based late‑delivery risk overlay for Bengaluru logistics
projects.summary: The system generates feasible last‑mile delivery routes while respecting hard capacity and time‑window constraints. An optional machine‑learning model predicts the risk of late delivery for each stop, allowing users to prioritize holds and re‑solve. It is intended for logistics teams planning daily vehicle schedules in Bengaluru.
projects.problem: Logistics operators need to create delivery routes that meet strict capacity and time‑window limits, and they also want early insight into which stops are likely to be delayed.
howItWorks: Scenario data is stored in a SQLite database and accessed via a FastAPI backend.
Travel times are obtained from OSRM; if OSRM is unavailable the solver falls back to haversine distance calculations.
Redis can cache OSRM matrices, weather data, and solve payloads, with an in‑memory fallback when Redis is down.
The optimizer uses OR‑Tools to solve a capacitated vehicle routing problem with time windows, never relaxing those constraints.
A scikit‑learn model trained on synthetic historical data provides a late‑risk probability for each stop, displayed in the UI.
The React/Vite frontend visualizes routes on Leaflet maps and allows users to hold stops and trigger re‑optimization.
highlights: Hard capacity and time‑window constraints are never relaxed; infeasible days produce a partial plan with a prioritized deferred list.
Automatic fallback to haversine travel matrix when OSRM service is unavailable.
Weather data from Open‑Meteo is used for risk context, with a safe offline stub if the service fails.
Optional Redis caching improves performance for travel matrices and weather lookups.

projects.title: AES-256-GCM Challenge Generator
projects.tagline: Browser‑based generator of AES‑256‑GCM encryption challenges for coding clubs
projects.summary: The app encrypts a user‑provided secret message with real AES‑256‑GCM using the browser's Web Crypto API. It then produces a set of cryptographic resources—key, IV, ciphertext, authentication tag, and a formatted challenge string—for participants to write their own decryption programs. It is intended for coding clubs that run cryptography or reverse‑engineering exercises.
projects.problem: Coding clubs need a reliable way to create authentic cryptographic challenges that use real encryption, preserve exact input formatting, and can be verified automatically without requiring a server or external tools.
howItWorks: The user enters a secret message in the web UI.
The app generates a random 256‑bit key and a 96‑bit IV with the browser's CSPRNG.
Using SubtleCrypto, it encrypts the message with AES‑256‑GCM, producing ciphertext and a 128‑bit authentication tag.
It concatenates IV, ciphertext, and tag, encodes the payload in Base64, and prefixes it with the version marker to form the challenge string.
A round‑trip decryption is performed locally to confirm the output matches the original input before displaying the resources.
All processing occurs client‑side; no data is sent to a server.
highlights: Real AES‑256‑GCM encryption via the native Web Crypto API, no simulated crypto.
Full Unicode support and exact whitespace preservation for diverse inputs.
Automatic round‑trip verification ensures the challenge is solvable before release.
Hand‑drawn UI using custom fonts, wobbly borders, and paper texture for a distinctive look.
Client‑only architecture eliminates storage or transmission of secret data.
35 automated Vitest tests covering Unicode handling, tampering detection, and format validation.

projects.title: EndeScript
projects.tagline: Secure AES‑256‑GCM message encryption web app
projects.summary: EndeScript encrypts and decrypts arbitrary text using AES‑256‑GCM. The encryption key resides only on the server, and messages are never stored. The interface is a minimal web UI built with Next.js.
projects.problem: People need a straightforward way to protect the contents of a message without handling cryptographic keys in the browser, while keeping the key out of client‑side code and storage.
howItWorks: The user sends plaintext to the POST /api/encrypt endpoint.
The server generates a fresh 12‑byte nonce and encrypts the data with AES‑256‑GCM using a server‑only key.
The ciphertext is returned in a versioned format "APP:v1:<base64url‑payload>".
For decryption, the user posts the ciphertext to POST /api/decrypt.
The server validates the format and version, then decrypts and returns the original text.
Both endpoints are limited to 30 requests per minute per IP using an in‑memory sliding‑window limiter.
highlights: Authenticated encryption with AES‑256‑GCM
Encryption key never leaves the server environment
Stateless processing; no message storage
Versioned ciphertext format supports future key rotation
In‑memory rate limiter protects the API
31‑test suite covering multiple languages, whitespace preservation, and error cases
Dockerfile for reproducible production builds

projects.title: GhostChat
projects.tagline: Anonymous, account‑free browser‑to‑browser chat using WebRTC
projects.summary: GhostChat is a web app that lets two browsers exchange messages directly over a WebRTC DataChannel. It requires no accounts, no server‑side storage, and persists chat history locally in IndexedDB. The UI is built with React and runs from a static Vite build.
projects.problem: Users who want private, ad‑free conversations often have to rely on services that store messages or require accounts, exposing metadata and content to third parties.
howItWorks: Each peer generates an anonymous identity and a short connection code.
PeerJS’s public cloud broker is used only for the initial SDP/ICE exchange needed to establish the WebRTC connection.
Once the DataChannel opens, all chat packets travel encrypted directly between browsers.
Messages are written to IndexedDB; an outbox store keeps unsent messages across page reloads.
A state machine monitors the channel, sending heartbeats and applying exponential backoff on reconnect.
Incoming packets are schema‑validated and duplicate‑protected before being stored.
highlights: Pure peer‑to‑peer messaging: no message server, no analytics, no third‑party scripts beyond PeerJS.
DTLS‑encrypted DataChannel ensures end‑to‑end confidentiality of chat content.
IndexedDB outbox guarantees pending messages survive refreshes and network interruptions.
Idempotent retransmission handling prevents duplicate display of messages.
Exponential backoff reconnection logic avoids connection storms.

projects.title: Vac.ai
projects.tagline: Hosted voice‑agent SaaS built on a small Rust engine
projects.summary: Vac.ai provides a hosted voice‑agent service built on a Rust engine. Customers access the service via an API and a web interface, while the platform integrates with telephony providers and payment processors.
projects.problem: Enterprises that need a continuously available voice‑agent platform often face high infrastructure costs and complex integration with telephony and payment services.
howItWorks: The core engine is written in Rust and runs as a Docker container on always‑on compute.
It connects to a PostgreSQL database and object storage (S3/R2) for persistence.
Voice generation uses the Gemini Live API keyed via VAC_GEMINI_API_KEY.
The service exposes HTTP endpoints for registration, login, agent management and live test calls.
Telephony streams are handled through Plivo and Twilio, and billing through Razorpay.
highlights: Engine written in Rust using async Axum and Tokio for high concurrency.
Deployment targets low‑memory always‑on containers (512 MB–1 GB).
Uses PostgreSQL via sqlx and object storage (S3/R2).
Integrates Gemini Live for voice, Plivo/Twilio for telephony, and Razorpay for payments.

projects.title: Mediscribe
projects.tagline: Patient-controlled health records with time-bounded clinician access
projects.summary: Mediscribe lets patients maintain a personal health record and grant doctors temporary access for a consultation. Doctors can view and edit the record during the session, and the updated information is saved back to the patient’s record after the visit.
projects.problem: Patients often have fragmented health records and limited control over who can view them, while clinicians need timely access during visits without retaining long‑term permissions.
howItWorks: A patient signs in, creates a 60‑minute access code or QR, and shares it with a doctor.
The doctor signs in, enters the code, and can view the patient’s authorized history for the duration of the session.
During the visit the clinician checks medication safety, updates prescriptions, and documents the encounter.
When the visit is completed, the system writes notes and medication changes to the patient’s record and revokes the doctor’s access.
The patient’s timeline, medication list, and consultation history update immediately.
highlights: Access tokens expire after 60 minutes or can be revoked when the visit ends.
QR payloads contain only a randomized identifier, never protected health information.
AI and medication lookups (OpenRouter, Groq, RxNorm, openFDA) run server‑side only.
Firestore and Storage security rules enforce that doctors must have a valid patient‑issued session.
Firebase Admin uses in‑memory storage with a /tmp fallback on Vercel.

projects.title: Lang.P
projects.tagline: A readable programming language designed for production use
projects.summary: Lang.P is a programming language with the .lp file extension, targeting both beginners and production environments. It provides a command‑line runner, a compiler, a language server, and a built‑in package manager. Documentation includes a full book, reference manual, and quick guides.
projects.problem: Many existing languages are either too low‑level for newcomers or lack the tooling needed for reliable production development.
howItWorks: The source code is processed by a lexer, parser, AST builder, and semantic analyzer written in Rust.
Compiled programs can be executed with the `lang` runner or built with the `langc` compiler.
A language server (`lang-lsp`) supplies editor integration for VS Code and Cursor.
A built‑in package manager (`lang`) reads a `langp.toml` manifest and installs modules such as the filesystem library.
Standard library modules are organized under a `stdlib` directory and can be imported with the `use` syntax.
highlights: Version 0.2 adds generic collections (List, Dict, Set, Tuple).
Beta support for objects with type definitions, methods, and inheritance.
Beta module system allowing `use` statements for standard library components.
Foundational package manager with lock file support.
